title: STEP 1 | WHY THE OBJECT MUST CHANGE

text: STEP 1 | WHY THE OBJECT MUST CHANGE
textPreview: STEP 1 | WHY THE OBJECT MUST CHANGE

text: AKM is complete only when every worker faces the same firm ladder
textPreview: AKM is complete only when every worker faces the same firm ladder

text:
AKM summarizes the firm side with a common premium and sorting with a worker-firm covariance. The displayed restriction is exactly what makes those two objects complete: every firm comparison is invariant across workers.

Once comparative firm advantages vary by worker, the coefficient vector is no longer the economic object. The primitive must be the full pairwise wage schedule.

text: STEP 2 | DECLARE THE PRIMITIVES
textPreview: STEP 2 | DECLARE THE PRIMITIVES

text: Observed matches and the target wage schedule are different objects
textPreview: Observed matches and the target wage schedule are different objects

text:
The target schedule assigns a maintained systematic wage to worker-firm pairs in a declared target set. The observed assignment distribution places mass only on realized edges; the product distribution breaks matching while preserving worker and firm marginals.

This distinction prevents an estimand from silently depending on missing cells or on a counterfactual assignment measure that was never stated.

text: STEP 3 | DEFINE THE FOUR TARGETS
textPreview: STEP 3 | DEFINE THE FOUR TARGETS

text: Four functionals replace the two AKM firm-side summaries
textPreview: Four functionals replace the two AKM firm-side summaries

text:
The first pair measures firm wage relevance: average cross-firm dispersion for a worker, and heterogeneity across workers in firm wage gaps. The second pair measures assignment: the change in wage-schedule variance under observed rather than independent matching, and the mean interaction selected by observed matches.

Under additivity, the gap-heterogeneity and mean-interaction targets vanish, while the remaining two collapse to the familiar AKM objects.

text: STEP 4 | PROJECT THE SCHEDULE
textPreview: STEP 4 | PROJECT THE SCHEDULE

text: A weighted two-way projection separates common levels from comparative advantage
textPreview: A weighted two-way projection separates common levels from comparative advantage

text:
The worker component is the worker's product-weighted average wage; the firm component is the common firm ladder; the interaction is what remains after both margins are removed. Row and column centering make this representation unique for the declared reference distributions.

This is an accounting projection of the wage schedule. It is not yet a causal or production decomposition.

text: STEP 5 | USE PROPOSITION 1
textPreview: STEP 5 | USE PROPOSITION 1

text: Uniqueness and orthogonality remove the cross terms
textPreview: Uniqueness and orthogonality remove the cross terms

text:
Suppose two centered decompositions represented the same schedule. Averaging their difference over firms identifies the worker component; averaging over workers identifies the firm component; subtraction then identifies the interaction. This proves uniqueness.

The same conditional mean-zero restrictions imply the displayed inner products are zero under product weights. Every variance identity that follows uses this orthogonality.

text: STEP 6 | DECOMPOSE FIRM RELEVANCE
textPreview: STEP 6 | DECOMPOSE FIRM RELEVANCE

text: Firm wage dispersion equals common-premium dispersion plus half of gap heterogeneity
textPreview: Firm wage dispersion equals common-premium dispersion plus half of gap heterogeneity

text:
For a fixed worker, only the common firm component and the interaction vary across firms. Orthogonality eliminates their covariance after averaging over workers.

A difference between two independently drawn firms doubles the interaction variance, so the gap-heterogeneity statistic is twice the interaction contribution. The ratio of half the gap statistic to total firm relevance is therefore the share that a common firm premium cannot summarize.

text: STEP 7 | DECOMPOSE ASSIGNMENT
textPreview: STEP 7 | DECOMPOSE ASSIGNMENT

text: Nonadditivity opens three assignment channels beyond AKM sorting
textPreview: Nonadditivity opens three assignment channels beyond AKM sorting

text:
Observed and product assignments have the same worker and firm marginals, so the marginal variances of the worker and firm components cancel. What remains is covariance between the common components, two covariances involving comparative advantage, and a change in interaction dispersion.

The first term is AKM-style sorting. The other three distinguish sorting on favorable cells from sorting on a common firm ranking.

text: STEP 8 | ISOLATE MEAN INTERACTION SELECTION
textPreview: STEP 8 | ISOLATE MEAN INTERACTION SELECTION

text: Breaking assignment leaves only the selected interaction mean
textPreview: Breaking assignment leaves only the selected interaction mean

text:
Because observed and product assignments share both marginals, the worker and common-firm means are identical under the two measures. Their difference therefore equals the observed mean of the centered interaction.

A positive value says realized matches occupy cells above what the two marginal components predict. It is a wage-schedule statement, not automatically a statement about output, surplus, or welfare.

text: STEP 9 | CHECK THE NESTED MODELS
textPreview: STEP 9 | CHECK THE NESTED MODELS

text: Additivity, Tukey interactions, and free factors impose distinct restrictions
textPreview: Additivity, Tukey interactions, and free factors impose distinct restrictions

text:
Additivity eliminates interaction-based firm relevance and assignment. A centered Tukey term ties comparative advantage to the same worker and firm indices that generate the main effects. A free-factor interaction permits a rank-one surface without forcing that economic interpretation.

Thus algebraic rank one does not by itself deliver a low-dimensional parameterization: unrestricted worker and firm factors can still be numerous incidental objects.

text: STEP 10 | STATE THE SUPPORT PROBLEM
textPreview: STEP 10 | STATE THE SUPPORT PROBLEM

text: The data reveal observed edges, while the targets generally use unobserved cells
textPreview: The data reveal observed edges, while the targets generally use unobserved cells

text:
The restriction operator selects the worker-firm cells present in the bipartite graph. Any perturbation in its kernel changes only missing cells and is observationally invisible without further structure.

Ordinary connectedness links worker and firm main effects in an additive model. It does not determine arbitrary cardinal levels or contrasts in missing pair-specific wage cells.

text: STEP 11 | APPLY PROPOSITION 4

text: A target is identified only when every missing-cell perturbation leaves it unchanged
textPreview: A target is identified only when every missing-cell perturbation leaves it unchanged

text:
For a linear target, the target loading must annihilate every direction hidden by the graph. For a quadratic target, both the linear cross term and the perturbation's own quadratic contribution must vanish over the admissible model class.

The paper's central firm and assignment statistics generally fail this test on an unrestricted incomplete schedule. With unbounded missing wages, some identified sets are unbounded.

text: STEP 12 | ADD THE MINIMAL STRUCTURE
textPreview: STEP 12 | ADD THE MINIMAL STRUCTURE

text: Low rank is imposed on comparative advantage, not on worker or firm main effects
textPreview: Low rank is imposed on comparative advantage, not on worker or firm main effects

text:
The additive components remain unrestricted; only the centered interaction is factorized. Setting the interaction matrix to zero nests AKM. Grouped BLM mean layers imply a low-rank double-demeaned interaction after type cells are lifted to workers and firms.

Kline-style mover restrictions concern edge differences rather than a complete level schedule, so they are diagnostics implied by this model, not a substitute for its level structure.

text: STEP 13 | EXPLOIT RECTANGLES
textPreview: STEP 13 | EXPLOIT RECTANGLES

text: Double differences identify factor contrasts after main effects cancel
textPreview: Double differences identify factor contrasts after main effects cancel

text:
Four observed cells forming a worker-by-firm rectangle eliminate the worker and firm components. Under rank one, the surviving double difference factors into a worker contrast times a firm contrast.

Overlapping rectangles transmit these relative contrasts across the graph. Anchors and normalizations fix the usual factor scale, sign, and location indeterminacies; sparse or rectangle-poor regions remain weakly identified.

Locally, unidentified tangent directions must lie in null directions of the target's derivative and curvature. This reframes the graph condition around the scalar being reported rather than around arbitrary factor normalizations.

text: Weighted low-rank least squares supplies fitted cells, but the estimands are quadratic operators

text:
Cell means are fit on observed edges using exposure weights and a fixed interaction rank. The four economic targets are then linear or quadratic functionals of the fitted schedule under the declared reference measures.

This distinction matters: an estimator with acceptable prediction error can still have material bias for a quadratic variance or covariance target.

text: STEP 16 | CORRECT QUADRATIC PLUG-IN BIAS
textPreview: STEP 16 | CORRECT QUADRATIC PLUG-IN BIAS

text: Estimation noise contributes its own positive quadratic term
textPreview: Estimation noise contributes its own positive quadratic term

text:
Sparse graphs create many noisy local worker, firm, and factor estimates. Even if the first-order term averages out, the noise quadratic need not vanish and can mimic genuine dispersion. This is the nonadditive analogue of limited-mobility bias.

A leave-worker-out or cavity construction estimates the relevant firm-side object without worker i and evaluates that worker against an object less mechanically correlated with the worker's noise.

text: STEP 17 | FORMULATE THE INFERENCE TARGET
textPreview: STEP 17 | FORMULATE THE INFERENCE TARGET

text: Consistency is required for aggregate functionals, not for every latent effect
textPreview: Consistency is required for aggregate functionals, not for every latent effect

text:
The relevant asymptotic sequence grows workers, firms, and observed edges together. Individual factors may remain noisy; the bias-corrected aggregate can still be consistent if leverage is controlled and support propagates enough information for the target.

Weak anchors, scarce rectangles, and high-leverage cells are therefore part of the inferential assumptions, not merely descriptive graph statistics. Rank uncertainty must also enter sensitivity analysis.

text: STEP 18 | MAKE THE DESIGNS DIAGNOSTIC
textPreview: STEP 18 | MAKE THE DESIGNS DIAGNOSTIC

text: Monte Carlo and empirical work should test recoverability, not only fit
textPreview: Monte Carlo and empirical work should test recoverability, not only fit

text:
Monte Carlo varies three ingredients jointly: the true interaction structure, assignment on common versus match-specific components, and graph support ranging from rectangle-rich to weakly anchored. It reports bias, RMSE, and coverage for each economic functional under rank misspecification.

The empirical application reports the firm-dispersion split, all four assignment channels, and support diagnostics including edge density, rectangle density, anchor strength, and target leverage.

text: STEP 19 | LOCATE THE CONTRIBUTION
textPreview: STEP 19 | LOCATE THE CONTRIBUTION

text: The adjacent literatures differ in the object they restrict
textPreview: The adjacent literatures differ in the object they restrict

text:
Kline and KSS characterize restrictions and bias for additive mover-edge effects; this note studies level functionals of a pairwise wage schedule. BLM's grouped mean layer motivates low-rank double demeaning, but complete BLM also models type probabilities and wage distributions.

Event-study diagnostics can validate restrictions on mover dynamics without eliminating nonadditive wage levels. Search and Roy models explain selected matches, but wage-schedule sorting alone does not identify production complementarity or surplus.

text: CONCLUSION | WHAT THE PAPER ADDS
textPreview: CONCLUSION | WHAT THE PAPER ADDS

text: The paper replaces coefficient interpretation with identified wage-schedule functionals
textPreview: The paper replaces coefficient interpretation with identified wage-schedule functionals

text:
The conceptual result is the displayed identity: total firm wage relevance separates into a common firm ladder and worker-specific firm-gap dispersion. The assignment decomposition then shows exactly how matching can operate through both components.

The econometric result is a roadmap: unrestricted sparse support cannot identify the cardinal quadratic targets; low-rank interaction structure can make the relevant functionals invariant; leave-out methods must then remove graph-induced quadratic bias. The remaining burden is a target-specific identification and inference theorem.
